references.name:
Ibn Khaldun,
  Al-Muqaddima
references.desc:
The foundational work of Islamic sociology
  and historical analysis; cyclical theory of
  civilizations

references.name:
Rashid al-Din,
  Universal History
references.desc:
First attempt at global history, compiled
  under Mongol patronage with an international
  research team

references.name:
Firdawsi,
  Shahnama
references.desc:
Persian national epic; status comparable to
  the Iliad; the foundation of New Persian
  literature

references.name:
Al-Ghazali,
  Revival of the Religious Sciences
references.desc:
The work that reconciled Sufi mysticism with
  Sunni orthodoxy, reshaping Islamic
  intellectual life

references.name:
Nizam al-Mulk,
  Siyasat-nama
references.desc:
Seljuk minister's handbook of governance,
  advocating strong central authority and the
  madrasa system

references.name:
Ibn Sina (Avicenna),
  Canon of Medicine
references.desc:
Medical encyclopedia that dominated European
  medical studies for centuries after Latin
  translation

references.name:
S.D. Goitein,
  A Mediterranean Society
references.desc:
Multi-volume study of the Cairo Geniza
  documents; Lewis credits the "intermediate
  civilization" concept

references.name:
Karl Jaspers,
  The Origin and Goal of History
references.desc:
Source of the "axial age" concept (600-300
  BCE) that Lewis applies to Middle Eastern
  religious development

references.name:
Charles Issawi,
  Economic History
references.desc:
Primary source for Lewis's economic data on
  the Ottoman Empire, Iran, and the Fertile
  Crescent

references.name:
Walter Bagehot,
  The English Constitution
references.desc:
Lewis applies Bagehot's "dignified vs.
  efficient" framework to the caliph-sultan
  relationship

references.name:
Lady Mary Wortley Montagu,
  Complete Letters
references.desc:
First-hand 18th-century observations of
  Ottoman society, especially the power of
  the ulema

references.name:
Ogier de Busbecq,
  Turkish Letters
references.desc:
Habsburg ambassador's account of Ottoman
  meritocracy and military discipline at its
  peak
